thread:
maya: Quick check — we're seeing flaky stream cancellations in the Node SDK when AbortController is used together with our retry layer. Anyone else hit this?

sam: yeah saw that. If you abort during a streaming response, the retry code sometimes kicks in and retries the whole request rather than failing fast.

jon: can you paste the minimal repro? most of our Node streaming code expects callers to close the stream, not abort mid-chunk.

maya: repro: create AbortController, pass signal into client.chat.stream(..., { signal }), then controller.abort() after first chunk. Behavior: client emits error then retry happens and we see duplicate partial outputs.

li: quick thought — our retry middleware currently wraps the whole request/response promise. For streaming we need a different contract: if signal.aborted -> stop retrying and propagate a CancellationError.

olivia: Agreed. Also Node's AbortSignal has the "abort" event — make sure our streaming transport unsubscribes listeners on cancel so we don't leak.

sam: in Python we model this with an \"AsyncClient.request(..., timeout=...)\" and rely on httpx's timeout + task.cancel(). But people do use contextlib.async_timeout and expect cancel to close the iterator. We added a patch that cancels the underlying httpx.stream but it's subtle.

jon: Go is different — we use context.Context. If ctx.Done() triggers mid-stream our goroutine returns and we cancel the lower-level http request. But we also have to ensure any buffered token cache usage doesn't re-enqueue the work for retry.

maya: thanks — two asks: 1) propose a cross-sdk cancellation contract snippet for docs/examples, 2) someone to review a small PR that changes retry for streaming to not retry on cancellation.

li: for (1) here's a short sample per-language that I think is clear: 
Node:
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const stream = await client.responses.stream({ model: 'rwd-small', prompt: 'hi' }, { signal: ac.signal });
// read some chunks...
ac.abort(); // should stop stream and not trigger retries
```
Python:
```py
import asyncio
async def run():
    async with client.responses.stream({ 'model': 'rwd-small' }) as stream:
        task = asyncio.create_task(stream.__anext__())
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        task.cancel()  # should cancel and not cause a retry
```
Go:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 100*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.ResponsesStream(ctx, params)
// canceling context should close stream and propagate error, no retry
```

olivia: that looks good. For docs we should explicitly state: "Abort/cancel signals are terminal for streaming requests — SDKs should not retry on user-initiated cancellation."

sam: PR note — when abort happens we should emit a distinct CancellationError type so caller code can detect user cancel vs network failure.

jon: agreed. Also add metrics: count of user_cancels vs stream_errors for SLOs. Helps product understand abandon rate.

maya: pasted PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 — changes: node retry middleware checks signal.aborted before scheduling retry, unsubscribes listeners, adds CancellationError.

devbot: deploy-checks triggered for branch sdk/stream-cancel-fix — lint OK, unit tests pending. :gear:

li: skimmed. One edge-case: if the server closes stream with EOF and user aborts simultaneously, order matters. We should prefer server-close semantics (i.e., treat server EOF as success if fully flushed).

sam: good catch. We'll add a small ordering test: simulate server EOF and immediate abort — ensure SDK returns server-complete rather than user-cancel if data ended.
